text:
Mia (Support): Hey team, customer acme-inc (acct acme-42) says we didn't actually apply the free-trial credits they were promised. I used the Support Console to grant 500 credits at 14:12 and the UI showed "Grant queued" but nothing reflected on their account. Ticket T-11234 linked: https://zendesk.example/tickets/11234

Alex (DevEx): Can you paste exact repro steps and any error messages you saw? Also was the console showing a 200/202 or a UI-only confirmation?

Mia (Support): Steps: 1) Open Support Console -> Users -> search acme-42 2) Click "Grant credits" -> enter 500 -> Submit. UI showed a toast: "Grant queued (request req_9f7b)". No follow-up activity. I ran a quick curl against the admin API afterwards:

```
POST /admin/api/v1/grants HTTP/1.1
Host: internal-api.prod.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer xxxxx
Content-Type: application/json

{"user_id":"acme-42","amount":500,"reason":"promo","request_id":"req_9f7b"}

Response: 202 Accepted
{"status":"queued","request_id":"req_9f7b"}
```

Mia (Support): I then checked the grants table and nothing with request_id=req_9f7b exists. Support console shows the action as "queued" but pending queue appears stuck. I attached the console screenshot in the ticket.

Raj (Eng-Infra): That smells like the backoffice worker couldn't reach payments-db or the job processor crashed after enqueuing. Can you share grants-service logs around req_9f7b? Also check Kafka topic "grant-queue" consumer lag.

Mia (Support): From grants-service logs (14:12-14:20):
```
ERROR grants-service: failed to apply grant req_9f7b: timeout waiting for payments-db: dial tcp 10.0.2.7:5432: i/o timeout
WARN grants-service: enqueued request req_9f7b to grant-queue
INFO grant-worker: picked up req_9f7b from grant-queue
ERROR grant-worker: processing req_9f7b failed: context deadline exceeded
```

Sophie (Billing): How many customers affected? Is this a single request or systemic? We need to know for compliance and to decide manual crediting vs rollback.

Mia (Support): I searched last hour and found 3 tickets with similar symptoms (different request_ids). All were manually attempted via Support Console between 14:08 and 14:20.

Alex (DevEx): Short-term workaround: we can apply the grant manually in DB with an idempotency guard. Example SQL (run from prod db-readwrite):
```
BEGIN;
INSERT INTO grants(user_id, amount, request_id, created_at, applied)
SELECT 'acme-42', 500, 'req_9f7b', now(), true
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM grants WHERE request_id='req_9f7b');
COMMIT;
```
Note: only UX team or infra oncall should run this. It will create the grant record so billing shows correctly.

Raj (Eng-Infra): I'll increase DB connection pool and check network path to payments-db. Also will check Kafka consumer group for grant-processor: run `kafka-consumer-groups --bootstrap-server kafka.prod:9092 --describe --group grant-processor` to confirm lag. If workers are failing due to DB timeouts, messages will be stuck in queue.

Sophie (Billing): We need audit logs for any manual DB insert. Please capture who runs the fix and add an audit entry in ticket. Compliance requires note of manual crediting.

Raj (Eng-Infra): I see a short outage to the payments-db node during that window (TCP resets, ~30s). Likely the grant-worker timed out and never retried with idempotency, leaving messages in Kafka with no successful commit. We'll restart grant-worker pods after increasing the DB timeout and patch the worker to use at-least-once semantics with idempotency on request_id.

Alex (DevEx): I'll open a PR to add idempotency checks in grants-service and an integration test for network blips. Also will add a small retry/backoff in worker.

Mia (Support): For now I'll apply the manual SQL for the 3 affected customers and update tickets with the audit snippet. Please confirm when grant-worker is restarted so I can clear the "queued" label in Support Console and notify customers.

deploy-bot: Started rolling restart of grants-service (actioned by Raj) to pick up timeout bump and consumer fix.

Raj (Eng-Infra): Restart completed, consumers rebalanced. Kafka lag drained for grant-queue. We'll keep monitoring for 30m.

Sophie (Billing): Thanks. Once Mia posts audit notes, I'll reconcile billing ledgers and mark the credits as approved.

Mia (Support): Thanks everyone — manual fixes applied for T-11234 and the two other tickets. Updated Zendesk with SQL audit and linked PR that will prevent recurrence. I'll follow up with customers to confirm credits visible.
